results.content: The mechanism analysis indicates that rural digital economy is more conducive to the non-agricultural employment, entrepreneurship, online learning behaviors, and human capital of high-income groups, thereby intensifying intra-rural income inequality. *H1: The development of the rural digital economy is more conducive to promoting the access of high-income groups to non-agricultural employment opportunities, which in turn exacerbates income inequality within the countryside*. Building on the above theoretical analyses, this paper explores the transmission mechanisms through which the development of the rural digital economy affects the intra-rural income inequality, focusing on three aspects: non-agricultural employment, entrepreneurship, online learning, and human capital. In light of this, this paper will further explore the mechanisms through which rural digital economy development affects intra-rural income inequality, focusing on non-agricultural employment, entrepreneurship, online learning, and human capital. The mechanism analysis shows that the development of the rural digital economy is more beneficial to the non-agricultural employment, entrepreneurship, and online learning behaviors of higher-income groups, thereby leading to increased intra-rural income inequality.
